ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Estimating per-instance information gain of a second view with a contrastive critic
PROPOSAL: Pretrain SimCLR with a ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 at batch size 128 for 400 epochs. For each image, define the gain of its second view as the critic log-ratio of the true partner minus the average log-ratio over the other views in the batch, and track it as an exponential moving average per instance. Use the gain to pick, among 4 candidate augmentation strengths, the one a view receives next. Linear-probe accuracy and the gain distribution are read at epochs 100, 200 and 400, with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Fixed standard augmentation recipe, random assignment of strengths with the same marginal frequencies, and a variant that selects by loss value instead of gain. Paired differences per seed are reported.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Gain-guided selection should lift linear-probe accuracy by 1 to 2 points at batch 128 over the fixed recipe. It fails if loss-based selection matches it, which would show that gain adds nothing beyond hard-example mining.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Following instance-level information gain through the whole course of pretraining
PROPOSAL: Pretrain MoCo v2 with a ResNet-50 on ImageNet-100 at 224 resolution for 800 epochs and save a snapshot every 10 epochs. At each of the 80 snapshots, estimate for all 126000 training images the gain of a view as the critic log-ratio of its true partner against 4096 queue negatives, averaging 16 augmentation draws per image. Fit a curve of gain against epoch per instance, cluster instances by curve shape, and compare the clusters with the final linear-probe error of each class, with 3 seeds. Report the curve shapes next to the error of each class, keep the cluster count fixed across seeds, and report the share of instances in each cluster.
CONTROLS: Gain calculated with a randomly initialised critic, clusters formed from loss trajectories alone, and a shuffled-label version of the cluster-to-error comparison.
COST: 300
PREDICTION: Curve clusters should separate classes of high and low final error, with correlation above 0.4. It fails if loss trajectories give clusters equally predictive of error.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A constrained view generator that adds diversity per instance
PROPOSAL: Train a small convolutional generator that maps each image to crop, colour and blur parameters, optimised to lower the contrastive agreement of the resulting view while a frozen momentum encoder keeps cosine similarity to the anchor above a fixed floor of 0.6. Pretrain a ResNet-18 on STL-10 at batch size 64 for 300 epochs, alternating encoder and generator updates every 2 steps. Evaluate by linear probe on STL-10 and by transfer to CIFAR-10, with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Standard SimCLR augmentations, a generator without the similarity floor, and a generator whose parameters are drawn from its own output histogram at random. Add a check that the floor binds on fewer than half of the instances.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: Probe accuracy should improve by about 2 points over the standard recipe at batch 64. Without the floor, semantic collapse is expected. The plan fails if the random-parameter control matches the learned generator.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Grid search of augmentation strength schedules for small-batch contrastive pretraining
PROPOSAL: Pretrain SimCLR with a ResNet-50 on ImageNet-100 at batch size 256 for 400 epochs under a grid of crop-scale minima from 0.08 to 0.5, colour-jitter strengths and blur probabilities: 24 configurations, each with 3 seeds. For each configuration record linear-probe accuracy, alignment and uniformity at three checkpoints, then fit a surface of accuracy over the strengths to locate the best trade-off between invariance and expressivity. Keep the seeds and the evaluation split fixed throughout, so that configurations differ only in their strengths.
CONTROLS: Surface fit compared with a flat fit and with a fit on shuffled configuration labels, and leave-one-configuration-out error reported.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: A ridge of best accuracy should appear at intermediate crop scale with strong colour jitter. It fails if the surface fit does not beat the flat fit on held-out configurations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Can instance-level view expansion replace big batches on ImageNet-100?
PROPOSAL: Pretrain SimCLR with a ResNet-50 on ImageNet-100 for 300 epochs with batch sizes 64, 256 and 1024 and a stock pipeline, and compare against batch size 64 where each image is expanded into 8 views produced by a learned view sampler that favours views with the highest estimated information gain. Report linear-probe and 20-shot accuracy, and the alignment and uniformity statistics of each run. Three seeds for the batch 64 settings and 2 for the rest.
CONTROLS: Stock pipeline at batch 64 with 8 views chosen at random, gradient caching to emulate batch 1024 at batch 64 hardware use, and a memory-queue variant with 16384 entries.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: Expansion at batch 64 should recover more than half of the gap between batch 64 and batch 1024 in linear-probe accuracy. It fails if random view selection recovers the same fraction.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pretraining on the full ImageNet with instance-level view expansion at three batch sizes
PROPOSAL: Pretrain MoCo v3 with a ViT-B/16 on ImageNet with its 1000 classes for 300 epochs at batch sizes 256, 1024 and 4096, each with a stock pipeline, and again with a gain-guided sampler that draws 8 views for each image. Evaluate by linear probe, 20-shot accuracy and transfer to 5 downstream datasets (Flowers, Pets, Food, Cars, Aircraft), and log alignment and uniformity every 20 epochs. Two seeds throughout. Report the share of the gap between the smallest and the biggest batch that expansion closes.
CONTROLS: Stock pipeline with 8 views chosen at random, a longer 600-epoch stock run at batch 4096, and a queue variant of 65536 entries.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The gain-guided sampler at batch 256 should land within 1.5 points of the stock batch 4096 run in linear-probe accuracy. It fails if the random-view control is within 0.5 points of the sampler.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Bias of contrastive mutual-information bounds as the batch shrinks
PROPOSAL: Draw paired Gaussian vectors in 64 dimensions with known mutual information of 2, 5 and 10 nats and train a small critic network to maximise InfoNCE on them with batch sizes 16, 32, 64, 128, 256 and 512. Compare the bound, which saturates at the logarithm of the batch size, with the known value, and test a leave-one-out variant and a learned-baseline variant that raise the ceiling in the small-batch regime. Report bias and variance of each estimator over 10 data draws.
CONTROLS: True mutual information as the reference, the plain InfoNCE bound, a nearest-neighbour estimator on the same samples, and a critic of different width to separate capacity from batch effects.
COST: 85
PREDICTION: Plain InfoNCE should be capped by the logarithm of the batch size, so the bias at 10 nats and batch 16 is large. The test fails if the learned-baseline variant shows the same cap.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mutual information between views of real images: an estimator study on frozen features
PROPOSAL: Extract 512-dimensional features with a frozen SimCLR ResNet-50 for 2 views of each CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, Tiny-ImageNet and ImageNet-100 training image. Estimate view-to-view mutual information with InfoNCE critics of 3 widths and 4 depths, MINE, and a nearest-neighbour estimator, at batch sizes 32 to 4096 in powers of 2. Compare how each estimator ranks the five datasets, with 5 random critic initialisations per cell. Report the rank correlation between each estimator's output and the known structure of the datasets, and plot bias against batch size for each critic width.
CONTROLS: A critic trained on shuffled view pairs, rankings from random-projection features of the same dimension, and rank agreement of estimators measured by Kendall correlation.
COST: 85
PREDICTION: Estimators should agree on dataset ranking above 0.7 once the batch exceeds 256. It fails if rankings keep changing with critic depth at the biggest batch.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Trading invariance against expressivity with a per-instance consistency weight
PROPOSAL: Pretrain a ResNet-50 with SimCLR on ImageNet-100 for 500 epochs where the invariance term of each pair is multiplied by a weight calculated from the instance's current information gain, lowered when gain is high so that rich views are not forced to agree fully. Compare a linear schedule, a gain-driven schedule and a learned schedule from a small network over the temperature values 0.1, 0.2 and 0.5. Read linear probe, nearest-neighbour accuracy and effective rank of embeddings, with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: A constant weight at the same mean, a weight drawn at random per instance, and the best of 5 constant weights chosen on the validation split. Report effect sizes with bootstrap intervals.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: The gain-driven schedule should raise embedding effective rank without losing probe accuracy. It fails if random weights give an equal rank gain, implying that the weight's content does not matter.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Characterizing the invariance and expressivity frontier of contrastive objectives on real images
PROPOSAL: Train SimCLR, MoCo v2, BYOL and Barlow Twins with a ResNet-50 on ImageNet for 400 epochs at batch size 512, varying the invariance weight in 6 steps and the crop-scale floor in 4 steps, 24 settings per method and 2 seeds. For each run calculate probe accuracy, embedding effective rank, alignment and uniformity at epochs 100, 200, 300 and 400, and draw one Pareto frontier of accuracy against rank per method. Plot accuracy against rank for each method and mark the setting that gives the best accuracy at a fixed rank.
CONTROLS: Frontier compared with a random-search frontier built from the same number of settings, and with a frontier from half the epochs.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Frontiers should differ by method, with contrastive methods showing a steeper accuracy loss as rank grows. It fails if the 200-epoch frontier orders methods identically to the 400-epoch one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Neighbourhood novelty of a view as a signal for per-instance augmentation
PROPOSAL: Define the novelty of a view for an instance as its mean cosine distance to the instance's own earlier views in a small per-instance bank of 8 embeddings, normalised by that instance's current alignment loss. Pretrain SimCLR with a ResNet-18 on Tiny-ImageNet at batch size 128 for 300 epochs, increasing augmentation strength for instances with low novelty and lowering it for instances with very high novelty. Evaluate by linear probe and kNN accuracy at epochs 100, 200 and 300, with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: Random strength assignment with the same distribution, novelty calculated on shuffled instance banks, and a loss-threshold rule with identical selection frequencies.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Probe accuracy should rise by 1 point or more over the stock recipe. It fails if the shuffled-bank control performs the same, since novelty would then carry no per-instance information.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Neighbourhood novelty of views measured at each epoch on four datasets
PROPOSAL: Calculate novelty of each view as mean cosine distance to a per-instance bank of 32 earlier embeddings, using a SimCLR ResNet-50 pretrained for 400 epochs on each of CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10 and Tiny-ImageNet, with a bank refresh at each epoch and 3 seeds. Relate the novelty trajectory of each instance to its final kNN correctness, and train a small predictor of final correctness from novelty summaries taken at four checkpoints. Keep the bank size and the refresh schedule identical for all four datasets and compare novelty histograms at the first and last checkpoints.
CONTROLS: Predictor from loss summaries only, from random bank contents, and from class label frequency alone; held-out AUROC is compared.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Novelty summaries should predict final kNN correctness with AUROC near 0.7, above loss summaries. It fails if class frequency alone reaches the same AUROC.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Feature-level view expansion by interpolating latent codes of augmented views
PROPOSAL: Add synthetic positives made by interpolating the embeddings of two augmented views of the same instance with a mixing coefficient drawn from a Beta distribution, then pass them through the projection head and contrastive loss. Pretrain a ResNet-50 with SimCLR on ImageNet-100 at batch size 128 for 300 epochs, comparing coefficient parameters 0.2, 0.5 and 1.0 and a variant that restricts mixing to instances with low estimated gain. Report probe accuracy and uniformity with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: No expansion at the same batch size, expansion using Gaussian noise of matched norm on embeddings, and mixing with views of other instances to test the semantic-consistency requirement.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Interpolation on low-gain instances should give a 1 to 2 point probe gain at batch 128. It fails if mixing with other instances is equal, showing that consistency was not the active ingredient.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latent interpolation of views evaluated on six pretraining recipes and five datasets
PROPOSAL: Create synthetic positives by interpolating the embeddings of two views of one instance, then evaluate this expansion inside SimCLR, MoCo v2, BYOL, SwAV, DINO and VICReg, using a ResNet-50 on ImageNet-100 for 400 epochs at batch size 256 and three mixing coefficients. Transfer each of the 18 pretrained models to CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Flowers, Pets and Food by linear probe, with 3 seeds. Report the alignment and uniformity of each model and the rank of each recipe by its change in accuracy relative to its own baseline.
CONTROLS: Each recipe without expansion, expansion using Gaussian noise, and a rank-ordering of recipes by gain from expansion compared with their baseline accuracy.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Gains should be largest for recipes with the weakest baseline uniformity. It fails if gains are uncorrelated with baseline uniformity across recipes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Relating view information gain to the spectrum of the augmentation graph
PROPOSAL: Build the augmentation graph over a 5000-image subset of CIFAR-10 by drawing 20 augmented views per image and connecting views whose embeddings are mutual 10-nearest neighbours under a SimCLR encoder pretrained to 4 different checkpoints. Calculate the 20 smallest Laplacian eigenvalues and the spectral gap at each checkpoint, and correlate them with the mean estimated gain per instance and with linear-probe accuracy. Use 5 random subsets and report the gap with bootstrap intervals over them.
CONTROLS: Graph built from random embeddings, from an untrained encoder, and from labels, which gives the ideal spectrum with exactly 10 near-zero eigenvalues.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: The spectral gap should widen as per-instance gain falls and probe accuracy rises. The test fails if the untrained encoder gives a similar correlation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Spectral clustering view of contrastive training on the full CIFAR-100 and Tiny-ImageNet graphs
PROPOSAL: Construct augmentation graphs with 50 augmented views per image for all 50000 CIFAR-100 images and all 100000 Tiny-ImageNet images, using a SimCLR ResNet-18 saved every 25 epochs of a 500-epoch run. Calculate the 100 smallest Laplacian eigenpairs per checkpoint and measure cluster purity of the spectral embedding against labels. Relate purity to linear-probe accuracy, with 3 seeds and different neighbourhood sizes. Plot the spectrum at the first and last checkpoint beside the purity curve.
CONTROLS: Purity from k-nearest-neighbour graphs of raw pixels, from random embeddings, and from a graph with edges permuted at random.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Purity should track probe accuracy with a correlation above 0.8. It fails if raw-pixel graphs reach similar purity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: A semantic-consistency filter for adaptively expanded views
PROPOSAL: Expand each instance into 4 views whose augmentation parameters are drawn from a learned distribution, and accept a view only if a frozen momentum encoder places it within a cosine radius of 0.7 of the anchor. Pretrain SimCLR with a ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 at batch size 64 for 400 epochs, with radii 0.5, 0.7 and 0.9 to expose the trade-off. Report probe accuracy, acceptance rate and the label purity of accepted views, with 3 seeds.
CONTROLS: No filter, a filter with a random acceptance of the same rate, and a filter based on a supervised classifier as an oracle for label purity.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: Filtering at 0.7 should keep accepted-view label purity above 90 percent and raise probe accuracy by about 1 point. It fails if the random filter equals the learned one.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Semantic consistency of adaptively drawn views on five datasets at six radii
PROPOSAL: Draw 8 views per instance from a learned augmentation distribution and keep those inside a cosine radius of the anchor, trying six radii between 0.4 and 0.9. Pretrain a ResNet-50 with SimCLR for 400 epochs at batch size 256 on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, STL-10, Tiny-ImageNet and ImageNet-100. Report probe accuracy, acceptance rate and accepted-view label purity per radius, with 3 seeds. Keep acceptance thresholds identical for the five datasets.
CONTROLS: No filter, random acceptance at matched rates, and an oracle filter using ground-truth labels on the first 500 instances.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: Purity should fall steadily as the radius grows, with best accuracy at an intermediate radius. It fails if accuracy is flat in the radius on all 5 datasets.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-instance gain from a two-view critic on a small image set
PROPOSAL: On a 10000-image subset of CIFAR-10, train a ResNet-18 with SimCLR at batch size 32 for 100 epochs and calculate, for each image, the gain of a fresh view as the drop in critic loss when that view is added to the anchor. Rank instances by gain at epochs 25, 50 and 100 and test whether the top quintile, once given stronger augmentation, improves linear-probe accuracy over giving it to a random quintile. Use 5 seeds.
CONTROLS: Random quintile selection, selection by anchor loss, and no strengthening, all at identical epochs and batch size.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: Strengthening the top-gain quintile should beat the random quintile by a half point or more. It fails if anchor loss selects the same instances in more than 70 percent of cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Per-instance gain from a two-view critic on the complete CIFAR-100 set and a ResNet-50
PROPOSAL: Train a ResNet-50 with SimCLR at batch size 128 on all 50000 CIFAR-100 images for 300 epochs and calculate, for each image, the gain of a fresh view as the drop in critic loss when it is added to the anchor, from 10 independent draws at six checkpoints. Test whether giving the top quintile stronger augmentation improves linear-probe and 10-shot accuracy over a random quintile. Use 3 seeds. Record the overlap between the quintiles chosen at different checkpoints.
CONTROLS: Random quintile selection, selection by anchor loss, and selection by gain calculated at epoch 50 only.
COST: 48
PREDICTION: The top-gain quintile should outperform the random one by a half point at each evaluation. It fails if epoch-50 gain performs equally well as gain recalculated at epoch 300.
